title: A private glass, a public death
text: Grant Larceny died after his private toast at 6:49. Botanical cardiac toxin was wiped inside his silver coupe before the cordial was poured. The glass tested clean when unwrapped at 6:40; food, decanter and pour tested clean. The service dome closed at 6:44, its seal remained intact until the witnessed 6:46 pour, and the glass was then watched through the toast. Contamination therefore occurred between 6:40 and 6:44. The missing conservation reference sample contains the same compound. One attending guest acted alone.

title: An evening of unfinished business
text: Grant’s papers concern a naming agreement, disputed objects, unpaid invoices, a trust and threats to careers. The warning note, suppressed reports, altered records and camera shutdown require investigation too. Preparation linen and the cabinet key were available to all registered gala guests; access alone does not identify a poisoner. Separate wrongdoing can explain why a guest conceals an activity. Compare what people say with the actual records before deciding which secret concerns the death.

title: Private service / movement statement
text: The salon camera was disconnected on Grant’s signed order. The glass arrived clean at 6:40. At 6:44 staff closed a transparent dome and watched its numbered seal continuously until the 6:46 pour; they then watched the glass until 6:49. No substance or substituted glass passed that protection. The contamination window is 6:40–6:44. Other rooms’ raw recordings, fixed-line transcripts and access logs have been recovered with the sixteen discoveries. Their clocks and continuous intervals are being authenticated. A timestamp alone does not place its owner at a device.

title: Recovered records / what they establish
text: Recovered sources are continuous, live and uncut; originals are preserved. The extracts certify occupied intervals and source integrity, but withhold identities and private contents. They do not certify who used a device. Match each guest’s account to the source: inside versus outside, live versus playback, fixed versus mobile. Wide films include exits; enclosure logs confirm locked rooms. Fixed-call terminals are ninety seconds each way from the salon, with no gap exceeding eighteen seconds. Portable props, automatic clips and shutter times alone prove no presence. The installation curtain locked at 6:38; the old cabinet was never installed.

title: Two clocks / a contaminated coupe
text: Museum linen carried the toxin onto the empty coupe. Shared key and linen access cannot identify its user. SECURITY-labelled records use synchronized time. BRASS-labelled overlays inherit the decorative gallery clock’s ten-minute error: 6:49–6:55 on those exports is 6:39–6:45 in real security time. The physical clock was not corrected before the gala. Compare the corrected interval, exact activity and recording source with each guest’s three statements. A genuine explanation can disclose misconduct while accounting for the contamination window. A denial or an unrelated timestamp does not do that.
